projects.title: Poker Trainer
projects.description: • Engineered a browser-based poker decision-math trainer in strict C++23, compiled to a single WebAssembly binary with an in-house WebGL2 renderer under Dear ImGui.• Structured the codebase as 14 dependency-ordered zones behind 16 interface headers sealed before implementation, keeping the dependency graph acyclic by construction.• Engineered a focus-reconciliation substrate giving an immediate-mode UI stable retained-mode keyboard navigation and modal traps; 2.5 ns/frame, zero heap allocation on the hot path.• Shipped end-to-end: custom digital art, manually verified poker formulas, Auth0 and Supabase accounts, and a deterministic MT19937_64 simulation exercised by 11,867 lines of native, browser-free tests.• Classified all 33,780 lines of source as domain versus platform cost; the decision math was under 4%, and published the analysis as a CppCon 2026 poster abstract.GitHub: https://github.com/daohhuynh/poker-trainerLive: https://poker-trainer-pearl.vercel.appAbstract: https://github.com/daohhuynh/poker-trainer/blob/main/docs/abstract.pdf

projects.title: OptiRisk
projects.description: Sub-Microsecond Quantitative Risk Engine• Engineered a sub-microsecond C++23 quantitative risk engine utilizing an LMAX Disruptor lock-free ring buffer with explicit L1 cache prefetching.• Architected an 8-lane AVX2 SIMD Black-Scholes pricing kernel, bypassing standard libraries to guarantee microsecond hardware-level throughput.• Built a custom binary wire protocol routing packed structs via UDP multicast and TCP to completely eliminate JSON serialization overhead.• Engineered a Python quantitative inference engine utilizing Gaussian Copulas and Sinkhorn-Knopp matrix balancingGitHub: https://github.com/daohhuynh/OptiRisk

projects.title: VIPER (Voltage Imaging Processing Execution Routines)
projects.description: Offline Pipeline for Voltage Image ProcessingArchitected an out-of-core memory accumulator utilizing Zarr and PyTorch MPS hardware acceleration, processing 100,000+ frame datasets while strictly bypassing system RAM constraints to prevent OOM crashes.Engineered an asynchronous I/O pipeline utilizing dedicated QThreads to decouple heavy TIF data ingestion from the UI, preventing main-thread blocking during large-scale processing.Enforced strict numerical stability by implementing float64 accumulation buffers and custom normalization algorithms to prevent precision overflow during the temporal averaging of float16 raw data.GitHub: https://github.com/daohhuynh/VIPER-Mac-Port
